topic: Binary Logic in the Towers of Hanoi
target_audience: High school students interested in computer science and discrete mathematics

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Language of Binary
lecture_lines: Each position represents powers of two.
Three bits count zero to seven.

sections.title: The Towers of Hanoi Rules
lecture_lines: Towers of Hanoi has three rods.
Only one disk moves at once.
Larger disks cannot cover smaller ones.
animations: Display three rods ([Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/rod.svg]) (Source, Auxiliary, Target) in #00FF00. Label them clearly.
Show animation of moving one disk ([Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/disk.svg]) between rods, highlighting the disk in #FF00FF.
Show error animation (disk collision) in #FF0000 when rule is violated.

sections.title: Mapping Binary to Moves
lecture_lines: Binary steps map to disk moves.
Disk one moves every odd step.
Disk two moves every two steps.
Disk three moves every four steps.
Binary counting guides the movement pattern.
animations: Show binary string (001) in #FFFFFF. Highlight moving disk [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/disk.svg] in #FF00FF.

Animate disk [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/disk.svg] 1 movement again. Shift binary count to (100). Highlight bit change.
Display overall mapping table of binary and disk [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/disk.svg] movement in #FFFFFF.

sections.title: Visualizing the Pattern
lecture_lines: Synchronization links binary to disk movement.
Three disks move in seven steps.
Total moves equal two to n minus one.
Patterns emerge from the binary count.
